questions.text: Which item belongs in source-safe pre-construction readiness?

options.text: Geotechnical and environmental investigation before committing to site and construction decisions
Painting the finished lobby after occupancy
Replacing as-built drawings with a brochure
Ignoring utility coordination until handover

questions.rationale: The CPM Handbook places technical investigations early in planning because they affect later design and construction.
questions.explanation: Design drawings show intent; as-builts show reality. Cost tracking uses different documentation (progress invoices, change orders). Preliminary drawings are pre-construction; as-builts are post-construction. As-builts reflect actual field conditions (substituted materials, MEP rerouting due to conflicts, rebar placement, as-installed dimensions). Accurate as-builts are critical for operations staff (HVAC maintenance, electrical troubleshooting), future renovations (understanding existing conditions), and legal disputes (damage claims, warranty issues). Discrepancies from design must be noted.

questions.text: What does PD 1096 RIRR require before constructing or altering a building or structure?

options.text: A building permit from the Building Official assigned to the place of work
Only an informal verbal approval
Only a furniture schedule
No permit if the contractor is experienced

questions.rationale: The checked PD 1096 locator states that construction, alteration, repair, moving, demolition, and similar work require a building permit.

questions.text: Which activity may be covered by an accessory permit under the checked PD 1096 scope?

options.text: Ground preparation, excavation, fencing, scaffolding, sign work, or demolition
Choosing desk lamps for occupancy
Selecting a brand slogan
Renaming a drawing file

questions.rationale: PD 1096 lists accessory permits for activities undertaken before or during building-permit processing.

questions.text: Why is utility coordination part of readiness?

options.text: Affected utilities and third parties may need lead time and information before relocation or coordination work
Utilities are only checked after final inspection
Utility location has no construction impact
Utility coordination is a substitute for permits

questions.rationale: The CPM Handbook emphasizes early and continuing utility and third-party coordination.
questions.code_citation: DENR DAO 2000-11 (Asbestos NESHAP); DOH AO 2001-004 (Lead Paint)

questions.text: Which document chain is source-safe for completion review?

options.text: Construction logbook, as-built plans, Certificate of Completion, and Certificate of Occupancy review
A marketing flyer only
A verbal promise that the work is finished
A construction photo without records

questions.rationale: PD 1096 ties completion and occupancy to signed records, as-built information, and inspection/review.
questions.code_citation: UAP SPP Document 202 General Conditions of Contract

questions.text: What should site layout planning consider before work begins?

options.text: Access, storage, accommodation, temporary services, plant, fencing or hoarding, and safety
Only the final color palette
Only social media content
Only interior furniture procurement

questions.rationale: Chudley/Greeno lists these as site layout considerations.

questions.text: What is a source-safe reason to conduct site selection and technical studies early?

options.text: Undesirable soil, contamination, and environmental impacts can create cost and schedule effects
Technical studies are only ceremonial
Site selection happens after occupancy
Soil conditions never affect projects

questions.rationale: The CPM Handbook links site selection and technical studies to cost, schedule, and buildability risk.

questions.text: Before excavation near adjoining property, which checked PD 1096 idea matters?

options.text: Protection of adjoining property and required notice before excavation
No notice or protection is ever relevant
Excavation is only a paint activity
Only interior designers can approve excavation

questions.rationale: PD 1096 permit conditions include notice and protection for adjoining property before excavation.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 uses 'final inspection' and 'Certificate of Completion/Occupancy'; punch list is contractual practice, not codified percentage.

questions.text: What is the LEA trap in pre-construction readiness questions?

options.text: Skipping source-checked legal, technical, access, utility, and closeout controls
Treating readiness as only furniture buying
Assuming permits are optional trivia
Ignoring as-built and logbook records

questions.rationale: The batch source scope connects readiness to investigations, permits, logistics, and completion records.

questions.text: Which statement avoids unsupported local-code expansion?

options.text: Use only PD 1096 and checked local raw sources for permit and occupancy claims in this batch
Invent new permit thresholds from memory
Use search snippets as primary law
Cite unverified section numbers without locators

questions.rationale: Batch 084 keeps legal/code claims inside local raw PDF evidence.
